title: Best Web Scraping Tools in 2026: 8 Platforms Compared
desc: The best web scraping tools in 2026 compared: Apify, Bright Data, Octoparse, Firecrawl and more, with real pricing, honest pros and cons, and who each is for.
keywords: best web scraping tools, best web scraping tools 2026, web scraping software, web scraping tools comparison, no-code web scraping, web scraping api, apify alternatives, best scraping tools for lead generation
cta: Want scraped, enriched leads without building the pipeline?
body:
Quick answer: for most people the best web scraping tool in 2026 is Apify, because its marketplace of more than 59,000 ready made scrapers means you rarely have to write any code, and the free plan gives you $5 of monthly usage with no credit card so you can test before you pay. If you need enterprise scale and the hardest anti bot sites, Bright Data wins. If you are not a developer, Octoparse is the friendliest. If you are feeding an AI model or agent, Firecrawl returns clean, ready to read data. Below we compare the eight tools we actually use and test, with pricing re verified against every vendor's own page on July 27, 2026, and the honest catch with each one.

Web scraping tools at a glance

Web scraping tools fall into three groups in 2026: no code platforms you point and click, marketplaces and APIs that handle the hard parts for you, and open source libraries you run yourself. Here is the short version of who each one is for and where pricing starts.

  • Apify: best all around. More than 59,000 ready made scrapers plus a real free tier. From $0, then $29 per month.
  • Bright Data: best for enterprise scale and tough, protected sites. Free tier of 5,000 records a month, pay as you go from $1.50 per 1,000 records, plans from $499 per month.
  • Octoparse: best no code desktop tool for non developers. Free plan, then $69 per month.
  • Firecrawl: best for AI and LLM ready output. Free 1,000 credits every month, then $16 per month.
  • ScraperAPI: best simple API for high volume. Free 1,000 credits, or a 7 day trial with 5,000, then $49 per month.
  • ScrapingBee: best lightweight API for small dev teams. 1,000 free credits to test, then $49 per month.
  • Browse AI: best no code monitoring and change alerts. Free tier of 50 credits a month, then $19 per month billed annually.
  • Crawlee: best free open source library for developers who want full control. Free.

1. Apify, best all around web scraping platform

Best for: almost everyone, from solo founders to data teams, especially if you would rather run a proven scraper than build one. Apify is a cloud platform whose Apify Store holds more than 59,000 prebuilt scrapers, called Actors, for Google Maps, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Amazon, and thousands of other sites. You can be pulling structured data within minutes of signing up, with no code.

Pricing (re verified July 2026): Free at $0 with $5 of monthly usage and no credit card, Starter at $29 per month, Scale at $199 per month, and Business at $999 per month, with 10 percent off on annual billing. Cost is usage based, billed in compute units (1 GB of RAM for one hour) at $0.20 per unit on the lower plans down to $0.13 on Business. Included Actor memory runs 16 GB on Free, 64 GB on Starter, 256 GB on Scale and 512 GB on Business. Students and startups can get 30 percent off, and Apify now supports x402 agentic payments, so an AI agent can run an Actor and pay per run without holding a subscription.

The catch: because pricing is usage based, your bill is hard to predict until you run a test, and unused monthly credits do not roll over. Heavy users also pay for proxies and data transfer on top.

For most readers it is the safest first stop. Start free on Apify and run a test scrape before you commit to a paid plan.

2. Bright Data, best for enterprise scale and tough sites

Best for: large teams scraping millions of pages, or sites with aggressive anti bot defenses. Bright Data runs one of the largest proxy networks in the world and pairs it with a Web Scraper API, a Web Unlocker, and a SERP API.

Pricing: there is now a free tier of 5,000 records a month, pay as you go runs $1.50 per 1,000 records, and the Scale plan is $499 a month for 384,000 included records, then $1.30 per 1,000 after that. Datacenter proxies start at $0.90 per IP and residential list at $5 per GB, currently discounted 50 percent to $2.50. The ready made scraper library covers more than 600 sites, and Bright Data only charges for records it delivers successfully.

The catch: it is built for scale, so the pricing, dashboard, and product sprawl can overwhelm a small team, and costs climb quickly. It is overkill if you only need a few thousand records a month.

3. Octoparse, best no code tool for non developers

Best for: people who want to scrape without writing code or thinking about proxies. Octoparse is a visual, point and click desktop app for Windows and Mac, with more than 500 ready made templates, built in IP rotation, and automatic CAPTCHA solving on paid tiers.

Pricing: a free forever plan covers 10 tasks and 50,000 rows of export a month. Standard is $69 per month and Professional is $249 per month on annual billing, which is 16 percent below monthly, adding cloud extraction and more concurrent tasks. Residential proxies are a $3 per GB add on, and every paid plan carries a 5 day money back guarantee.

The catch: the desktop app has a learning curve of its own, cloud runs are limited on lower tiers, and very complex or heavily protected sites can still trip it up.

4. Firecrawl, best for AI and LLM ready data

Best for: developers and AI teams who want a page turned into clean markdown that a language model can read. Firecrawl handles JavaScript, CAPTCHAs, and anti bot detection, then returns tidy, structured output built for retrieval and agents.

Pricing: 1,000 free credits every month, then Hobby at $16 per month for 5,000 pages, Standard at $83 for 100,000, Growth at $333 for 500,000 and Scale at $599 for a million, all billed yearly. Scrape, crawl, map and monitor cost one credit per page, and search costs two credits per ten results.

The catch: there is still no pay as you go plan, and credits do not roll over, with auto recharge credits and custom annual plans the only exceptions. It is focused on AI use cases more than general purpose scraping at huge scale.

5. ScraperAPI, best simple API for high volume

Best for: developers who just want one API endpoint that handles proxies, browsers, and CAPTCHAs, then returns the HTML. You send a URL, you get the page back.

Pricing: 1,000 free credits to start, or a 7 day trial with 5,000, then Hobby at $49 per month for 100,000 credits, Startup at $149 for one million, Business at $299 for three million, Scaling at $475 for five million, and Professional and Advanced tiers at $975 and $1,975. Annual billing takes 10 percent off. ScraperAPI publishes its real credit costs: a standard page is 1 credit, Amazon is 5, Google and Bing are 25, LinkedIn is 30, and bot protected sites add 10 on top.

The catch: credits do not carry over, and the credit cost per request climbs steeply on hard sites, since one LinkedIn page costs 30 times a plain one, so your effective price per page is often far higher than the headline rate suggests.

6. ScrapingBee, best lightweight API for small teams

Best for: small developer teams who want a clean, well documented API and headless browser rendering without managing any infrastructure.

Pricing: 1,000 free credits with no card, then Freelance at $49 per month for 250,000 credits, Startup at $99 for one million, Business at $249 for three million and Business Plus at $599 for eight million. A request costs from 1 credit for plain HTML and rises with JavaScript rendering, premium proxies or AI extraction. ScrapingBee charges only for successful requests and is SOC 2 Type II audited.

The catch: the per credit model means JavaScript and premium proxy requests eat credits fast, so a plan that looks generous can run out sooner than expected on protected sites.

7. Browse AI, best no code monitoring and alerts

Best for: non technical users who want to watch specific pages and get alerted when something changes, like a competitor price or a job listing. You train a robot by clicking through a page once.

Pricing: a free plan with 50 credits a month across 2 websites, Personal at $19 per month billed annually (12,000 credits granted upfront for the year, or $48 if you pay monthly), Professional at $69 per month annually for 60,000 credits a year, and a managed Premium tier from $500 a month. One credit extracts 10 rows of data or captures one screenshot.

The catch: credits burn quickly, because a 50 item listing page costs 5 credits before you touch a single detail page, protected sites carry a 2 to 10 credit minimum per run, and nothing rolls over at the end of the cycle. It is built more for monitoring and small extractions than for scraping millions of rows.

8. Crawlee, best free open source library

Best for: developers who want full control and no platform fees, and are happy to host and maintain their own scrapers. Crawlee is a free, open source Node.js and Python library, maintained by Apify, that handles queues, retries, and anti blocking patterns for you.

Pricing: free. You only pay for your own servers and any proxies you add.

The catch: you build and maintain everything yourself, including proxy rotation and scaling. There is no dashboard and no support line, so it costs engineering time instead of subscription dollars.

What changed since we published this in June 2026

We first published this comparison on June 16, 2026 and re verified every vendor against its own pricing page on July 27. Six things had moved, and three of them were our own numbers being wrong. We have corrected them in the open rather than quietly editing them out.

  • Apify's Store grew from about 36,000 Actors to more than 53,000 by July 2026, and to 59,065 when we re-checked on 12 August 2026. Apify publishes the live count on its own store page, and this is the number in this article that had drifted furthest.
  • Firecrawl's free tier got much better, and we had it wrong. We described 500 one time credits. Firecrawl now gives 1,000 credits every month, and the $16 Hobby plan covers 5,000 pages rather than 3,000. There is also a Standard tier at $83 for 100,000 pages that we had missed entirely.
  • ScrapingBee is cheaper than we said. We listed Startup at $149 and Business at $599. The real 2026 prices are $99 and $249, with $599 now buying the far larger Business Plus tier, and there is a free 1,000 credit trial we had not mentioned at all.
  • Bright Data added a free tier of 5,000 records a month, and its $499 Scale plan includes 384,000 records, not the "roughly half a million" we estimated.
  • ScraperAPI publishes its real credit costs, so we replaced our vague "1 to 75 credits" with the published table: 1 credit for a standard page, 5 for Amazon, 25 for Google or Bing, 30 for LinkedIn, and 10 more on bot protected sites.
  • Every serious tool here now ships an MCP server. Apify, Bright Data, ScrapingBee and Octoparse all expose their scrapers to AI agents, and Apify has gone further with x402 payments so an agent can pay per run with no human subscription behind it. In June, agent access was an Apify differentiator. By July it is table stakes.

The rankings are unchanged. Three of those corrections make a competitor look better than we originally described, and we have still left the order alone, because none of them changes the job each tool is best at. A more generous Firecrawl free tier does not turn it into a marketplace of ready made scrapers, and a cheaper ScrapingBee still ships no scrapers at all. Apify keeps the top slot on the job most readers actually have, which is wanting a working scraper today.

How to choose the right web scraping tool

Match the tool to who is using it. If you are not a developer, start with Octoparse or Browse AI. If you are a developer who wants speed, a marketplace like Apify or a simple API like ScraperAPI or ScrapingBee will save you days. If you are feeding an AI model, Firecrawl returns the cleanest output. If you are scraping at enterprise scale or hitting walls on protected sites, Bright Data is built for it. And if you want zero platform cost and have engineers, Crawlee is free.

Whatever you pick, always test on a small run first so you can see the real per page cost, and budget for proxies on harder sites. If you would rather skip the tooling entirely, our team can build and run the whole pipeline for you as part of our AI automation and lead generation services.

From scraped data to booked meetings

Scraping is only step one. The real value shows up when clean data flows into a system that turns it into revenue: enrich the records, verify the emails, then run a disciplined outreach sequence. That is exactly the workflow we build for clients. Scrape with a tool like Apify, enrich and verify, then send through a deliverability safe cold email system.

faqs: What is the best web scraping tool in 2026?

For most people it is Apify, because its marketplace of more than 59,000 prebuilt scrapers means you rarely write code, and the free plan lets you test with no credit card. Developers working at enterprise scale often prefer Bright Data, and non developers tend to like the point and click simplicity of Octoparse.
What is the best free web scraping tool?

Apify and Octoparse both have genuine free tiers, Apify with $5 of monthly usage and Octoparse with 10 tasks and 50,000 rows a month. Firecrawl now gives 1,000 credits every month and Bright Data 5,000 records. For developers, Crawlee is fully open source and free to self host, though you still pay for your own servers and any proxies you use.

Scraping publicly available data is generally legal in many regions, but it depends on the website's terms, the type of data, and local laws such as the GDPR. Avoid scraping personal or copyrighted data without a lawful basis, respect robots rules and rate limits, and seek advice for anything sensitive. This is general information, not legal advice.
Which web scraping tool is best for AI and LLMs?

Firecrawl is purpose built for this, returning clean markdown that a language model can read directly. Apify also runs an MCP server and now accepts x402 agentic payments, so an agent can trigger and pay for a scraper on its own. By mid 2026 Bright Data, ScrapingBee and Octoparse all ship MCP servers too, so the question is less which tool an agent can call and more which one hands back the cleanest data.
How much do web scraping tools cost in 2026?

Entry paid plans range from about $16 a month for Firecrawl Hobby and $19 for Browse AI to $49 for ScraperAPI and ScrapingBee and $69 for Octoparse, while Apify starts at $29 and keeps a free tier. Bright Data now has a free tier of 5,000 records a month, and its Scale plan is $499. Most tools bill by credits or usage, so run a small test first to learn your real cost.
Do I need to know how to code to scrape websites?

No. No code tools like Octoparse and Browse AI let you scrape by pointing and clicking, and Apify's marketplace runs prebuilt scrapers for you. Coding only becomes necessary when you need fully custom logic, which is where a library like Crawlee or an API like ScraperAPI helps.
